requirements.evidence: Queues is implemented in app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:61-65 (mount authorizes create), :80-96 (create via CreateQueue, slug derived by the action), :131-153 (rename with Str::slug), :169-176 (toggle through UpdateQueue), :203-220 (scoped accessQueue/accessGrants); the serve panel is in app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:48-98 (mount, mode validation, scoped queue lookup, exception-to-notice mapping, rate limit); members tabs are in resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:6-20; routes are at routes/web.php:58-59; both lang files define the contract keys (for example lang/en/ui.php has 'nav_queues' => 'Queues' and lang/pt_BR/ui.php has 'nav_queues' => 'Filas'). Minor gap: resources/views/livewire/entity/serve.blade.php:58-60 renders the priority badge only when priority > 0, so normal tickets show no priority even though the task lists priority among the waiting-list fields.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through the existing actions (Queues.php:88, :140-145, :173, :248; Serve.php:83); #[Validate] is used on name/renameName (Queues.php:27, :51) and mode (Serve.php:37); policies/gates are used at Queues.php:63, :69, :82, :102, :118, :135, :159, :182 and Serve.php:50, :122, :138; docs and changelog are updated (CHANGELOG.md:9, docs/business-rules.md:492); views use x-label/x-input and {{ }} escaping. One clear deviation: three public Queues actions do not call $this->authorize() themselves (Queues.php:169-173, :193-200, :243-249).

security.evidence: Client ids are re-resolved scoped to the entity in Queues.php:100, :116, :133, :157, :171, :180, :245-246 and Serve.php:72, :134-136; Entity and lastCalledTicketId are #[Locked] (Queues.php:24-25; Serve.php:28-29, :43-44); name/renameName/mode are validated; Blade output is escaped with {{ }}. Gap: toggleActive(), grantAccess() and revokeAccess() rely on UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess for authorization instead of calling $this->authorize() in the Livewire action (Queues.php:169-173, :193-200, :243-249), which violates the project's mandatory Livewire policy; the domain actions currently prevent unauthorized writes, so the impact is limited.

tests.evidence: QueuesPageTest.php:128-140 is the only unauthorized-call test and covers only create; :244-278 covers access grants/revokes and audit logs; :280-311 covers foreign-id tampering; :313-341 covers tampered modal ids; :343-353 covers aria-labels. ServePanelTest.php:46-51 covers non-members, :210-221 covers foreign queue ids, :223-234 covers callNext without a grant, and :249-253 covers the locked lastCalledTicketId. Members tests cover the default tab, the invites tab and invalid tab names. Missing: unauthorized-call tests for rename, toggleActive, openAccess, grantAccess and revokeAccess, which the conventions require for each Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: The components reuse the existing domain actions (Queues.php:5-7, Serve.php:5) rather than adding a service or repository layer; helpers are small and local (Queues.php:227-259, Serve.php:132-158); no speculative abstractions or duplicated business rules.

readability.evidence: Names and comments are clear (Queues.php:35-38, :46-49, :54-57; Serve.php:31-34, :40-42); methods are focused; the view markup mirrors the existing members page (queues.blade.php:5-27, serve.blade.php:45-66).

scope.evidence: The diff only adds the queues/serve feature, the members tabs, the navbar links, both locales, routes, the related docs and tests (routes/web.php:58-59; CHANGELOG.md:9; docs/business-rules.md:492; resources/views/layouts/default-page.blade.php:641-648). No unrelated refactors or domain changes.

issues.explanation: toggleActive(), grantAccess() and revokeAccess() resolve the queue/membership scoped to the entity but never call $this->authorize(); they rely on UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess. The project's Livewire policy requires every public action to authorize the resolved model server-side, so this must be fixed even though the actions currently prevent unauthorized writes.

Only create has an unauthorized-call test; rename, toggleActive, openAccess, grantAccess and revokeAccess have no test that a non-manager session is denied, although the conventions require an unauthorized-call test for each Livewire action.
The waiting list renders the priority badge only when priority > 0, so normal tickets (priority 0) show no priority, while the task requires the list to show code, priority, issue time and channel.

review.summary: The change adds the queues management page (create, rename, deactivate/reactivate, per-queue access grants) and the attendant serve panel (queue/mode selectors, waiting list, call next with notices and rate limiting), plus routes, navbar entries, pt_BR/en texts, docs and extensive Pest tests. It is functionally complete, but three public Queues actions skip the explicit $this->authorize() required by the project's Livewire security policy, and the unauthorized-call tests for those actions are missing. The waiting list also omits the priority for normal tickets; these need changes before merging.
